title: Compose Phases, Snapshot Reads, and Skippable Work Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies compose phases, snapshot reads, and skippable work?
options: Place state reads in the narrowest honest phase, preserve stable identity contracts, and optimise from release trace evidence.
Use debug recomposition counts as final proof
questions.answer: Place state reads in the narrowest honest phase, preserve stable identity contracts, and optimise from release trace evidence.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: Any Compose state change necessarily reruns composition, layout, and draw for the entire screen.
questions.explanation: Annotating a mutable model as Stable to reduce recomposition violates the runtime contract and can prevent required UI updates.

questions.prompt: Why can a draw-phase state read be cheaper than a composition read?
questions.answer: Its invalidation can rerun drawing without rebuilding composition or geometry when those outputs are unchanged.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
